l4Discriminating.text: Data are generated, replayed, or selectively perturbed by an external process; readings are not real-time instrument outputs — The core evidence cluster remains intact and is reinforced by today's readings. This is the signature of either a finite-precision algorithmic sequence (drawn uniformly without replacement from a finite set, then perturbed by independent noise or shuffling) or a pseudorandom generator with very high period. A real continuous analog sensor exhibits either frequent accidental repeats (due to low effective resolution) or no repeats with much larger spacing; the combination of zero repeats and extreme spacing precision is implausible for honest analog measurement. (2) Today's Day 23 spike in resonator_lab variability (SD ~0.027, nearly 5× the post-baseline SD ~0.0056) is the first sharp excursion, but it occurs on a day when resonator_obs and pendulum_obs also spike, despite these instruments being physically isolated. (3) The lack of zero-lag correlation despite identical physical measurands (pendulum period and resonator frequency both report on the same gravitational/elastic environment) is explained only if the four streams are independent algorithmic sequences, offset by design to create spurious lag-correlations. This becomes testable: if external perturbation is real, today's spike should persist in cross-correlation structure tomorrow—e.g., the resonator_lab spike should correlate with resonator_obs at a non-zero lag. (4) Post-baseline drift signs are inconsistent (pendulum_lab +0.0053, resonator_lab +0.0018, pendulum_obs -0.0007, resonator_obs +0.0011 in ∆-from-baseline terms), arguing against a single environmental driver or a common calibration reference.
